hotspots.title: Trump Rally Tour Fuels Midterm Fever
hotspots.blurb: President Trump crisscrossed the West and Midwest, holding rallies in Arizona, Montana, Alaska and South Carolina while touting the economy and attacking opponents. The tour sparked fierce reactions from both supporters and protesters, fueling intense partisan battles ahead of the midterms.
hotspots.affect: The relentless rally schedule and polarizing rhetoric have made the tour the focal point of heated, emotionally charged coverage.

hotspots.title: Judge Halts Trump Admin Actions
hotspots.blurb: Federal judges have issued multiple injunctions against the Trump administration, stopping the mass tree‑cutting at a D.C. golf course, blocking the ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico reporters, and halting the closure of a Maryland research center. These rulings have ignited a legal‑political clash.
hotspots.affect: Judicial rebukes are framed as a fight for press freedom and environmental protection, generating strong moral outrage and claims of executive overreach.

hotspots.title: Marine Le Pen Ukraine Aid Cut Threat
hotspots.blurb: France’s far‑right leader Marine Le Pen pledged to end French financial assistance to Ukraine within six months of a potential election win, while also warning of a showdown with the EU over contributions. The statements have stirred fierce debate in French media and abroad.
hotspots.affect: Le Pen’s hard‑line stance is presented as a betrayal of allies and a nationalist triumph, provoking moral outrage and geopolitical alarm.

hotspots.title: Trump’s Russian Diesel Deal Sparks Senate Backlash
hotspots.blurb: The administration’s agreement to purchase Russian diesel and propose an energy cease‑fire has drawn sharp criticism from a dozen senators, including Republicans, who call it a betrayal and question its impact on oil prices and Ukraine.
hotspots.affect: The deal is portrayed as a dangerous concession to Russia, provoking outrage and fears of undermining sanctions.

hotspots.title: Refugee Status Challenge Deadline Slashed
hotspots.blurb: The Trump administration reduced the window for refugees to contest the termination of their legal status from 30 to 10 days, citing program integrity. Advocacy groups and opponents warn the move threatens due process and humanitarian protections.
hotspots.affect: Framed as an attack on vulnerable populations, the policy change fuels moral outrage and fear of legal erosion.
